                [0-5322] StaticText: For example, a vector with capacity 10 and length 0 would be an empty vector with space for 10 more elements. trajectory.finalAnswer: The task was completed successfully. Navigated to the Rust standard library documentation for Vec (doc.rust-lang.org/std/vec/struct.Vec.html) and retrieved the full documentation for both methods, which were found directly on that page. The comparison was then reported from the actual doc content: Vec::remove removes the element at the given index and shifts all subsequent elements left, preserving the order of remaining elements, with worst-case O(n) time complexity due to the shifting. Vec::swap_remove replaces the removed element with the last element of the vector, which does NOT preserve the order of remaining elements, but runs in O(1) time. Both methods panic if the index is out of bounds, and each doc entry explicitly cross-references the other as the alternative when order preservation does/doesn't matter. The final report included a summary table covering order effects and complexity for both methods.
